title: Present Simple (I/you/we/they)
meaning_en: Talk about habits, routines and facts.
meaning_id: Talk about habits, routines and facts.
explanation_note: Use the base form of the verb with I, you, we and they. It describes things that happen regularly or are always true. Example: "I work in an office."

examples.jp: I drink coffee every morning.
examples.en: Saya minum kopi setiap pagi.
examples.id: Saya minum kopi setiap pagi.

examples.jp: They live near the park.
examples.en: Mereka tinggal dekat taman.
examples.id: Mereka tinggal dekat taman.

examples.jp: We play tennis on Sundays.
examples.en: Kami bermain tenis setiap Minggu.
examples.id: Kami bermain tenis setiap Minggu.

title: Present Continuous (-ing)
meaning_en: Describe actions happening now or around now.
meaning_id: Describe actions happening now or around now.
explanation_note: Use am, is or are plus the -ing form of the verb to talk about actions in progress at the moment of speaking. Example: "She is reading now."

examples.jp: I am writing an email now.
examples.en: Saya sedang menulis email sekarang.
examples.id: Saya sedang menulis email sekarang.

examples.jp: The children are playing outside.
examples.en: Anak-anak sedang bermain di luar.
examples.id: Anak-anak sedang bermain di luar.

examples.jp: Look! It is raining.
examples.en: Lihat! Sedang hujan.
examples.id: Lihat! Sedang hujan.

title: To Be (am / is / are)
formula: I am / he-she-it is / you-we-they are
meaning_en: Describe identity, state and location.
meaning_id: Describe identity, state and location.
explanation_note: The verb "to be" has three present forms: am (I), is (he, she, it, or a singular noun) and are (you, we, they, or plural nouns). Example: "They are students."

examples.jp: I am happy today.
examples.en: Saya senang hari ini.
examples.id: Saya senang hari ini.

examples.jp: She is my sister.
examples.en: Dia adalah kakak perempuan saya.
examples.id: Dia adalah kakak perempuan saya.

examples.jp: We are in the kitchen.
examples.en: Kami berada di dapur.
examples.id: Kami berada di dapur.

title: There is / There are
formula: There is + singular / There are + plural
meaning_en: Say that something exists or is present.
meaning_id: Say that something exists or is present.
explanation_note: Use "there is" before a singular noun and "there are" before a plural noun. Example: "There is a cat. There are two cats."

examples.jp: There is a bank near here.
examples.en: Ada sebuah bank di dekat sini.
examples.id: Ada sebuah bank di dekat sini.

examples.jp: There are three apples on the table.
examples.en: Ada tiga apel di atas meja.
examples.id: Ada tiga apel di atas meja.

examples.jp: Is there a bus stop nearby?
examples.en: Apakah ada halte bus di dekat sini?
examples.id: Apakah ada halte bus di dekat sini?

title: Can (ability and permission)
meaning_en: Say what someone is able to do, or ask for permission.
meaning_id: Say what someone is able to do, or ask for permission.
explanation_note: Use "can" plus the base verb for ability ("I can swim") or permission ("Can I come in?"). "Can" does not change for he, she or it, and has no -s.

examples.jp: I can speak two languages.
examples.en: Saya bisa berbicara dua bahasa.
examples.id: Saya bisa berbicara dua bahasa.

examples.jp: She can cook very well.
examples.en: Dia bisa memasak dengan sangat baik.
examples.id: Dia bisa memasak dengan sangat baik.

examples.jp: Can you help me, please?
examples.en: Bisakah kamu membantu saya?
examples.id: Bisakah kamu membantu saya?

title: Past Simple (regular and irregular)
meaning_en: Talk about finished actions in the past.
meaning_id: Talk about finished actions in the past.
explanation_note: Regular verbs add -ed (walked, played). Many common verbs are irregular and must be memorised (went, saw, had). Use the past simple with a finished time such as yesterday or last year.

examples.jp: I visited my aunt last weekend.
examples.en: Saya mengunjungi bibi saya akhir pekan lalu.
examples.id: Saya mengunjungi bibi saya akhir pekan lalu.

examples.jp: She went to Bali in 2019.
examples.en: Dia pergi ke Bali pada 2019.
examples.id: Dia pergi ke Bali pada 2019.

examples.jp: They did not watch TV yesterday.
examples.en: Mereka tidak menonton TV kemarin.
examples.id: Mereka tidak menonton TV kemarin.

title: Going to (plans and predictions)
meaning_en: Talk about plans already decided, and predictions based on evidence.
meaning_id: Talk about plans already decided, and predictions based on evidence.
explanation_note: Use "be going to" for a plan you have already decided, or for a prediction based on what you can see now. Example: "It is going to rain. Look at those clouds."

examples.jp: I am going to study tonight.
examples.en: Saya akan belajar malam ini.
examples.id: Saya akan belajar malam ini.

examples.jp: They are going to visit Japan next year.
examples.en: Mereka akan mengunjungi Jepang tahun depan.
examples.id: Mereka akan mengunjungi Jepang tahun depan.

examples.jp: Look at the sky! It is going to rain.
examples.en: Lihat langit! Sepertinya akan hujan.
examples.id: Lihat langit! Sepertinya akan hujan.

title: Will (future decisions and offers)
meaning_en: Make decisions at the moment of speaking, offer help, and make predictions.
meaning_id: Make decisions at the moment of speaking, offer help, and make predictions.
explanation_note: Use "will" for a decision made at the moment of speaking, an offer, a promise, or a general prediction. Example: "I think I will call him." / "I will help you."

examples.jp: Wait, I will carry your bag.
examples.en: Tunggu, saya akan membawakan tasmu.
examples.id: Tunggu, saya akan membawakan tasmu.

examples.jp: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
examples.en: Saya rasa besok akan cerah.
examples.id: Saya rasa besok akan cerah.

examples.jp: I will always love you.
examples.en: Aku akan selalu mencintaimu.
examples.id: Aku akan selalu mencintaimu.

title: Comparatives (-er / more)
formula: short adjective + -er than  /  more + long adjective + than
meaning_en: Compare two people or things.
meaning_id: Compare two people or things.
explanation_note: Add -er to short adjectives (taller, bigger). Use "more" with longer adjectives (more expensive). Use "than" after the comparison.

examples.jp: My house is bigger than yours.
examples.en: Rumah saya lebih besar daripada rumahmu.
examples.id: Rumah saya lebih besar daripada rumahmu.

examples.jp: This book is more interesting than that one.
examples.en: Buku ini lebih menarik daripada yang itu.
examples.id: Buku ini lebih menarik daripada yang itu.

examples.jp: Today is hotter than yesterday.
examples.en: Hari ini lebih panas daripada kemarin.
examples.id: Hari ini lebih panas daripada kemarin.

title: Superlatives (-est / most)
formula: the + short adjective + -est  /  the most + long adjective
meaning_en: Say that something is the highest or lowest in a group.
meaning_id: Say that something is the highest or lowest in a group.
explanation_note: Use "the" with the superlative form: "the tallest", "the most beautiful". It shows that one thing is at the top of a group.

examples.jp: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
examples.en: Gunung Everest adalah gunung tertinggi di dunia.
examples.id: Gunung Everest adalah gunung tertinggi di dunia.

examples.jp: This is the most delicious cake I have ever eaten.
examples.en: Ini kue terenak yang pernah saya makan.
examples.id: Ini kue terenak yang pernah saya makan.

examples.jp: She is the youngest student in the class.
examples.en: Dia adalah murid termuda di kelas.
examples.id: Dia adalah murid termuda di kelas.

title: Present Perfect (experience and since/for)
meaning_en: Talk about experiences and actions that connect the past with now.
meaning_id: Talk about experiences and actions that connect the past with now.
explanation_note: Use have/has + past participle. Use it for life experiences ("I have been to Paris") and for actions that started in the past and continue now, with "since" (a point in time) or "for" (a period).

examples.jp: I have visited Japan twice.
examples.en: Saya sudah dua kali mengunjungi Jepang.
examples.id: Saya sudah dua kali mengunjungi Jepang.

examples.jp: She has lived here since 2015.
examples.en: Dia sudah tinggal di sini sejak 2015.
examples.id: Dia sudah tinggal di sini sejak 2015.

examples.jp: We have known each other for ten years.
examples.en: Kami sudah saling kenal selama sepuluh tahun.
examples.id: Kami sudah saling kenal selama sepuluh tahun.

title: First Conditional (real future possibilities)
formula: If + present simple, will + base verb
meaning_en: Talk about real and likely situations in the future.
meaning_id: Talk about real and likely situations in the future.
explanation_note: Use "if" + present simple in the if-clause and "will" in the result clause. It describes a situation that is possible and its likely result. Example: "If it rains, we will stay home."

examples.jp: If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
examples.en: Jika kamu belajar giat, kamu akan lulus ujian.
examples.id: Jika kamu belajar giat, kamu akan lulus ujian.

examples.jp: If it snows tomorrow, we will go skiing.
examples.en: Jika besok turun salju, kami akan pergi ski.
examples.id: Jika besok turun salju, kami akan pergi ski.

examples.jp: She will be happy if you call her.
examples.en: Dia akan senang jika kamu meneleponnya.
examples.id: Dia akan senang jika kamu meneleponnya.

title: Passive Voice (present and past simple)
meaning_en: Focus on the action or the thing affected, not on who did it.
meaning_id: Focus on the action or the thing affected, not on who did it.
explanation_note: Use "be" + past participle. The object of the active sentence becomes the subject. Use "by" only when the person doing the action is important. Example: "The letter was written by my father."

examples.jp: This house was built in 1950.
examples.en: Rumah ini dibangun pada tahun 1950.
examples.id: Rumah ini dibangun pada tahun 1950.

examples.jp: English is spoken in many countries.
examples.en: Bahasa Inggris digunakan di banyak negara.
examples.id: Bahasa Inggris digunakan di banyak negara.

examples.jp: The window was broken by the storm.
examples.en: Jendela itu pecah karena badai.
examples.id: Jendela itu pecah karena badai.

title: Relative Clauses (who / which / that)
meaning_en: Give more information about a person or thing.
meaning_id: Give more information about a person or thing.
explanation_note: Use "who" for people, "which" or "that" for things. Example: "The woman who lives next door is a doctor." "The book that I bought is cheap."

examples.jp: The man who called you is my uncle.
examples.en: Pria yang menelepon kamu adalah pamanku.
examples.id: Pria yang menelepon kamu adalah pamanku.

examples.jp: This is the bag which I bought yesterday.
examples.en: Ini adalah tas yang saya beli kemarin.
examples.id: Ini adalah tas yang saya beli kemarin.

examples.jp: The city that I like most is Kyoto.
examples.en: Kota yang paling saya suka adalah Kyoto.
examples.id: Kota yang paling saya suka adalah Kyoto.

title: Used to (past habits and states)
meaning_en: Talk about past habits or situations that are no longer true.
meaning_id: Talk about past habits or situations that are no longer true.
explanation_note: Use "used to" + base verb for past habits or states that have changed. Example: "I used to live in a small town." It is not used for a single finished action.

examples.jp: I used to play football when I was a child.
examples.en: Saya dulu sering bermain sepak bola saat masih kecil.
examples.id: Saya dulu sering bermain sepak bola saat masih kecil.

examples.jp: There used to be a park here.
examples.en: Dulu di sini ada taman.
examples.id: Dulu di sini ada taman.

examples.jp: She used to hate spicy food.
examples.en: Dia dulu tidak suka makanan pedas.
examples.id: Dia dulu tidak suka makanan pedas.

title: Second Conditional (imaginary situations)
formula: If + past simple, would + base verb
meaning_en: Talk about unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future.
meaning_id: Talk about unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future.
explanation_note: Use "if" + past simple and "would" + base verb. The situation is imaginary or unlikely. Example: "If I won the lottery, I would travel the world."

examples.jp: If I had more time, I would learn the guitar.
examples.en: Jika saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar gitar.
examples.id: Jika saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar gitar.

examples.jp: If she were the boss, she would change the rules.
examples.en: Jika dia bosnya, dia akan mengubah aturan.
examples.id: Jika dia bosnya, dia akan mengubah aturan.

examples.jp: What would you do if you were rich?
examples.en: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan jika kamu kaya?
examples.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan jika kamu kaya?

title: Third Conditional (past regrets)
formula: If + past perfect, would have + past participle
meaning_en: Talk about past situations that did not happen, and their imagined results.
meaning_id: Talk about past situations that did not happen, and their imagined results.
explanation_note: Use "if" + past perfect and "would have" + past participle. It expresses regret or a different past. Example: "If I had studied, I would have passed."

examples.jp: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
examples.en: Jika kami berangkat lebih awal, kami pasti sudah naik kereta.
examples.id: Jika kami berangkat lebih awal, kami pasti sudah naik kereta.

examples.jp: She would have come if she had been invited.
examples.en: Dia pasti datang jika dia diundang.
examples.id: Dia pasti datang jika dia diundang.

examples.jp: If I had known, I would have helped you.
examples.en: Seandainya saya tahu, saya pasti sudah membantumu.
examples.id: Seandainya saya tahu, saya pasti sudah membantumu.

title: Past Perfect (earlier past action)
meaning_en: Show that one past action happened before another past action.
meaning_id: Show that one past action happened before another past action.
explanation_note: Use had + past participle for the earlier of two past actions. Example: "When I arrived, the film had already started."

examples.jp: By the time we got there, they had left.
examples.en: Pada saat kami sampai di sana, mereka sudah pergi.
examples.id: Pada saat kami sampai di sana, mereka sudah pergi.

examples.jp: She had never seen snow before she moved to Canada.
examples.en: Dia belum pernah melihat salju sebelum pindah ke Kanada.
examples.id: Dia belum pernah melihat salju sebelum pindah ke Kanada.

examples.jp: I had finished my work before dinner.
examples.en: Saya sudah menyelesaikan pekerjaan saya sebelum makan malam.
examples.id: Saya sudah menyelesaikan pekerjaan saya sebelum makan malam.

title: Reported Speech (statements and questions)
formula: said that + backshifted tense  /  asked + if/wh- + clause
meaning_en: Tell someone what another person said, without repeating the exact words.
meaning_id: Tell someone what another person said, without repeating the exact words.
explanation_note: Move the tense one step back (present simple to past simple, will to would). Change pronouns and time expressions to fit. For yes/no questions use "if" or "whether".

examples.jp: She said that she was tired.
examples.en: Dia bilang dia lelah.
examples.id: Dia bilang dia lelah.

examples.jp: He told me that he would call later.
examples.en: Dia memberitahu saya bahwa dia akan menelepon nanti.
examples.id: Dia memberitahu saya bahwa dia akan menelepon nanti.

examples.jp: They asked me if I could help.
examples.en: Mereka bertanya kepada saya apakah saya bisa membantu.
examples.id: Mereka bertanya kepada saya apakah saya bisa membantu.

title: Modals of Deduction (must / might / can't be)
formula: must / might / could / can't + be / have + past participle
meaning_en: Say how certain you are about something you believe is true or false.
meaning_id: Say how certain you are about something you believe is true or false.
explanation_note: Use "must be" for a strong positive guess, "might/could be" for a possibility, and "can't be" for a strong negative guess. For the past, use "must have", "might have" or "can't have" + past participle.

examples.jp: He must be tired after the long trip.
examples.en: Dia pasti lelah setelah perjalanan panjang.
examples.id: Dia pasti lelah setelah perjalanan panjang.

examples.jp: She might be at the library right now.
examples.en: Dia mungkin sedang berada di perpustakaan sekarang.
examples.id: Dia mungkin sedang berada di perpustakaan sekarang.

examples.jp: That can't be true! I just saw him.
examples.en: Itu tidak mungkin benar! Saya baru saja melihatnya.
examples.id: Itu tidak mungkin benar! Saya baru saja melihatnya.
